gap: No result ChatGPT got states how the feeders mount on a pole: Birdfy's pole-top adapter for the Feeder Metal 2 4K takes poles up to 1.08 in (27.4 mm) across, while Birdbuddy's universal pole mount, which comes in the box with the Home and Nook Solar, needs a pole with a 0.97 in (2.5 cm) inner diameter and does not include the pole.
standout_why: I opened Reviewed (cited), PlumageDispatch (#5) and Feeder Field (#3). WIRED's cited page and wired.com could not be fetched here. Reviewed gives no pole sizes; it says only 'sturdy, high pole' for the Metal 2 4K and 'can be mounted on a pole' for the Birdbuddy Home. PlumageDispatch and Feeder Field state no pole diameters. Reviewed and Feeder Field already say the Feeder 2 series has no microSD. PlumageDispatch already says Birdbuddy's Alexa link is a paid-plan feature. PlumageDispatch and Feeder Field already describe Birdfy's two AI editions, though neither gives a price difference. None of the three says that Birdfy sells one solar panel line for all its feeders, with a Y-splitter on the 5 W and 8 W versions. None mentions Birdfy's add-on exclusions either.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Every main candidate fits a standard 1-inch feeder pole, so a shopper who already has a pole can choose on camera and subscription. A thicker pole won't take the Metal 2 4K adapter, which tops out at 27.4 mm. It also adds two cost points against Birdbuddy: Alexa needs Premium, and the Nook Solar is 2.4 GHz only. Our page's 'Free for life' AI cell holds only for Birdfy's 'AI Lifetime Free' edition, because the 'AI by Subscription' edition gets a 7-day trial and then needs a plan. The page should name the edition beside the price.
